# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 74 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 74 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_074_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Part 1 — The Great Rock and the Twelve Mountains

**74:1** After I had written down the commandments and similitudes of the shepherd, the angel of repentance, he came to me and said: "I want to show you all the things the Holy Spirit spoke with you in the form of the church. For that Spirit is the Son of God."

**74:2** "For you were weak in the flesh, and the truth had not yet been explained to you. Speak with the Power and it will come to you more clearly, because that Power is strong and divine and belongs to glorious and mighty virtue."

**74:3** I said to him: "Lord, I beg you to show me all the things you promised to show me." And he led me away to Arcadia, to a certain hill, and seated me on the hill. And he himself stood before me.

**74:4** And I saw a great plain, and around the plain twelve mountains, each having a different form. The first mountain was all black rock. The second was bare, with no vegetation at all. The third was full of thorns and brambles. The fourth had vegetation that was half-withered — the upper parts of the plants were green but the roots were dry, and some plants were withered because the sun had scorched them. The fifth mountain had green grass but was rugged. The sixth mountain was full of clefts, some small and some large, and in the clefts there was grass.

**74:5** The seventh mountain had cheerful vegetation, and the whole mountain was blooming, and all kinds of cattle and birds fed on that mountain; and the more the cattle and birds fed, the more the vegetation flourished and abounded. The eighth mountain was full of springs, and every kind of creature of the Lord drank from those springs.

**74:6** The ninth mountain had no water whatsoever and was entirely a wilderness, and it was full of wild beasts and deadly reptiles that destroyed human beings. The tenth mountain had great trees and was entirely shaded, and beneath those trees sheep lay resting and ruminating.

**74:7** The eleventh mountain was covered densely with trees, and those trees were laden with various kinds of fruit, so that anyone who saw them would desire to eat of their fruits. The twelfth mountain was entirely white and its appearance was radiant and joyful, and the mountain itself was very beautiful in form.

---

*LOGOS renders according to the Greek text of P.Mich. 130 with attention to the visionary structure and the twelve-mountain typology that frames Similitude 9.*
